Jeremy Bentham

Quotes / Jeremy Bentham / Q0191

English

It is the greatest happiness of the greatest number that is the measure of right and wrong.
Thinker Jeremy Bentham
School Utilitarianism
Source A Fragment on Government, Preface (1776)
Theme Happiness
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with A Fragment on Government, Preface (1776), within the tradition of Utilitarianism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of happiness, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Jeremy Bentham's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
